source.title: Kuramoto Oscillatory Phase Encoding: Neuro-inspired Synchronization for Improved Learning Efficiency
source.authors: Mingqing Xiao; Yansen Wang; Dongqi Han; Caihua Shan; Dongsheng Li

record.file_problem: The full paper is present; some figure and table text is garbled, but the relevant numeric phase-synchronization results are stated in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines phase synchronization within a model and downstream vision-language performance, but does not test whether independently trained models' representations become more similar with scale or capability.
record.gate_note: No reported result directly compares representation geometry across independently trained models, tracks cross-model similarity with scale or performance, or tests interchangeability or recurrence of features across models. The within-model, same-entity phase-synchronization measurements are related but do not test any listed version; they are recorded under fits_no_version. Vision-language classification and retrieval results are downstream performance measures, not measurements of cross-model representational convergence.
record.test_reason: The study proposes KoPE, a phase-synchronization mechanism for ViTs, and reports task performance and within-model phase synchronization. It never compares representations across independently trained models, seeds, modalities or scales, and never maps one model's representations onto another's. It does not engage the Platonic Representation Hypothesis or convergent learning even as a tool, so 'cites_only' or T6 fits better than 'discusses'. Its CLIP-style 'representation alignment with language' is reported only as zero-shot accuracy and retrieval, not as a cross-model alignment score.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that adding Kuramoto phase dynamics to ViTs improves training, parameter and data efficiency. They report gains on segmentation, CLIP zero-shot performance and ARC-AGI. They claim nothing about cross-model convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: The phase initialization changes learning dynamics: random initialization performs worse, while 2D rotary initialization learns faster. The paper reports similar performance across tested coupling types and a range of γ values.

fits_no_version.finding: In ViT+KoPE, phase synchronization among tokens of the same entity rises from layer 0 to layer 11 on ADE20K and COCO, more so for mixed phases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KoPE phase states for same-entity tokens become more synchronized with depth.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306 (2026)
record.problems: No evidence on cross-model representational convergence. The relevant synchronization measurements concern same-entity tokens within a KoPE model and do not compare models or similarity metrics.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were omitted. Downstream classification and retrieval scores, attention-concentration measurements, and segmentation or reasoning results do not measure cross-model representational convergence.

untested.parts: No cross-model representational similarity measured at any scale.
CLIP training reports zero-shot accuracy and retrieval only; no vision-language alignment metric tracked against model quality.
No stitching, linear mapping or relative-representation tests.
No similarity-metric or input dependence analysis.
No analysis of alignment plateaus or of their causes.

record.verdict_notes: The 'vision-language alignment' wording refers to downstream CLIP zero-shot performance, not to a representational alignment metric, so it does not bear on V2. The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only' or T6 because the paper never discusses the convergence claim.

versions.untested_parts: No cross-model representation comparison across model size or capability.
No measure of how paired image-caption representation alignment changes as both models improve.
No comparison of models trained from different initializations.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No test for recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
No comparison of cross-model convergence across similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
No test of convergence plateaus, incompleteness, or effects of shared training data or objectives on cross-model alignment.
